new_design: Preserve every existing ordered worklist and launch, but relabel GPU node-indexed metadata rows into level/kind execution order. All N rows remain, including inactive tail, so lengths/payload/capacity and original CUDA stay unchanged. Remap only node-ID values in worklists/edges/children; retain physical reach/CFV/action offsets and every floating value bit. CPU public tree/save IDs remain unchanged. This is not CTA sorting, arity packing or CFV/reach layout tuning.
prospective_memory_route: During construction, reuse the two completed CPU plan reach_src vectors as forward/inverse scratch (the constructor uploads reach_slot, not reach_src). Reuse the existing pinned staging window for typed metadata copies, with length/alignment checks and original-layout fallback. For compact ArenaLayout records, investigate storing the device node ID in existing record padding for lock updates. No new retained node-map allocation is admitted by this design. Actual record/host layout, full-path integration and peak/capacity/material proof remain mandatory.
caller_risks: All original node-ID arrays and tree.children values must be transformed by a total bijection; positional children_start offsets and physical row IDs must not be remapped.

Lock replacement must preserve CPU node IDs, exact sigma order and GPU metadata semantics, including unsupported/manual inputs. Compact record lookup and a supported original-layout fallback need full validation.

Experimental symmetric/paged/stored projection callers can bind CPU node IDs outside the ordinary kernels. They need explicit correct mapping or a prospective original-layout constructor fallback; no silent exclusion or compatibility claim.
Repacking adds CPU work and can worsen runtime even when address footprint shrinks. Original D183 phase times remain excluded; only full fresh solve timing can establish gain.
next: Freeze a CPU-only reversible mapping/footprint model and actual private-record layout ability before any source prototype. Any literal history hit must be classified before novelty/admission.
reference_limits: NVIDIA coalescing rules concern warp accesses. Across-CTA footprint counts below will not be called transactions, misses, scheduling evidence or a speedup.
